name: Microsoft Defender

source.title: Azure services in FedRAMP audit scope

description: Endpoint protection and detection included with many Microsoft 365 plans.

extensions.name: Defender Vulnerability Management
extensions.detail: Built-in exposure and patch priority on the same agent.

extensions.name: Defender for Identity
extensions.detail: Detect identity-based attacks on Active Directory.

extensions.name: Security Copilot
extensions.detail: AI assistant and agents for investigation, hunting, and summaries across Defender, Sentinel, and Entra.
extensions.pricingNote: Billed in Security Compute Units. Microsoft 365 E5 includes a monthly allowance of 400 SCUs per 1,000 licences, rolling out from November 2025.

pricingSource.title: Security Compute Units included with Microsoft 365 E5

compete.wins: Often already licensed with Microsoft 365. Vulnerability management and identity detections sit on the same agent.
compete.loses: A weaker fit when the estate is not mostly Microsoft, or when you want a vendor-operated SOC.

name: CrowdStrike
description: Cloud-native EDR with a strong threat-intel graph and optional managed detection.

extensions.name: Falcon Complete
extensions.detail: CrowdStrike-operated monitoring, triage, and containment.

extensions.name: Falcon Spotlight
extensions.detail: Vulnerability assessment from the Falcon agent.

extensions.name: Charlotte AI
extensions.detail: Generative and agentic AI for triage, investigation, and natural-language search in Falcon.
extensions.pricingNote: Credit-based. CrowdStrike says qualifying customers get 50 AI credits a month at no cost; heavier use needs more credits.

compete.wins: Strong threat-intel graph, and Falcon Spotlight covers vulnerabilities without a second agent.
compete.loses: High cost. It does not improve the control if Defender is already licensed and staffed.

name: SentinelOne
description: Autonomous endpoint protection that can roll back ransomware changes.

extensions.name: Vigilance MDR
extensions.detail: SentinelOne managed detection and response.

extensions.name: WatchTower
extensions.detail: Threat hunting and intelligence add-on.

extensions.name: Purple AI
extensions.detail: AI analyst for natural-language hunting, investigation summaries, and agentic investigation.
extensions.pricingNote: Agentic investigation opened to all customers in June 2026 as a free trial; continued use draws down paid Singularity Credits.

pricingSource.title: SentinelOne opens Purple AI agentic investigation to all customers

compete.wins: Can roll an endpoint back after ransomware without waiting on an analyst.
compete.loses: A third console if Falcon or Defender is already the operating EDR.

name: Huntress
description: Managed EDR aimed at small IT teams that do not staff a SOC.

extensions.name: Managed ITDR
extensions.detail: Identity threat detection for Microsoft 365 tenants.

extensions.name: Managed SIEM
extensions.detail: Huntress-operated log pipeline for smaller estates.

compete.wins: A managed service for a small team that will not staff a SOC.
compete.loses: Not the product for a large estate with its own 24/7 detection team.

name: Microsoft Sentinel

source.title: Azure services in FedRAMP audit scope
Sentinel geographical availability and data residency

description: Cloud SIEM and SOAR on Azure, priced by ingestion and retention.

extensions.name: UEBA
extensions.detail: User and entity behavior analytics on the same workspace.

extensions.name: Automation rules
extensions.detail: Rules that triage, assign, and run playbooks on incidents without a separate SOAR.
extensions.pricingNote: Playbooks run on Azure Logic Apps, which Azure bills separately.

pricingSource.title: Azure Logic Apps for Sentinel playbooks

extensions.name: Security Copilot
extensions.detail: AI assistant and agents for investigation, hunting, and summaries across Defender, Sentinel, and Entra.
extensions.pricingNote: Billed in Security Compute Units. Microsoft 365 E5 includes a monthly allowance of 400 SCUs per 1,000 licences, rolling out from November 2025.

pricingSource.title: Security Compute Units included with Microsoft 365 E5

compete.wins: Stays inside Azure and can automate response without a separate SOAR.
compete.loses: The bill follows ingestion. A noisy estate gets expensive fast.

name: Wazuh
description: Open-source XDR and SIEM for teams that can run the platform themselves.

extensions.name: Wazuh Cloud
extensions.detail: Hosted deployment when you do not want to operate the indexer.

compete.wins: No license fee if the team can run the platform.
compete.loses: You own the uptime, the parsers, and the on-call. That is the cost.

name: Splunk Enterprise Security

source.title: Splunk Cloud Platform attains FedRAMP High

description: SIEM built on the Splunk data platform, with detection, investigation, and SOAR in one workflow. Self-hosted or cloud.

compete.wins: Very flexible search and a large library of detections and integrations. A common choice for large SOCs.
compete.loses: Expensive at volume, and the search language and data onboarding need skilled staff.

extensions.name: Splunk SOAR
extensions.detail: Playbook automation and case response paired with Enterprise Security.
extensions.pricingNote: Included in the Premier edition, not Essentials.

extensions.name: UEBA
extensions.detail: User and entity behaviour analytics for insider and compromised-account detection.

extensions.name: AI Assistant for Security
extensions.detail: Natural-language help for investigations and searches.
extensions.pricingNote: Both editions; Essentials on Splunk Cloud only.

name: Google Security Operations
description: Cloud-native SIEM and SOAR (formerly Chronicle) with Google threat intelligence built in.

compete.wins: Built for large log volumes, with long retention and fast search across it.
compete.loses: A cloud-only service, and the most value comes to teams already comfortable in Google Cloud.

name: Elastic Security

source.title: Elastic Cloud Hosted achieves FedRAMP High

description: SIEM, endpoint protection, and analytics on Elasticsearch. Self-managed or Elastic Cloud. Elasticsearch and Kibana offer an AGPL licence option alongside Elastic's own licences.

compete.wins: A free self-managed starting point with real search power, and a path to a paid managed service.
compete.loses: Running Elasticsearch at scale is real work, and several advanced features need a paid subscription.

sources.title: Elastic adds AGPL licence option (Business Wire)

name: Exabeam
description: SIEM with behavioural analytics. New-Scale is the cloud-native platform; LogRhythm SIEM is the self-hosted option after the 2024 merger.

compete.wins: User and entity behaviour analytics is the strength, useful for insider and account-takeover cases.
compete.loses: Two product lines after the merger. Check which one a quote is for and what its roadmap is.

name: Microsoft Entra ID

source.title: Azure services in FedRAMP audit scope
Entra ID data storage for European customers

description: Workforce identity for Microsoft estates, from free MFA up through conditional access.

extensions.name: ID Protection
extensions.detail: Risk-based sign-in detections and automated response.
extensions.pricingNote: Risk-based policies need Entra ID P2.

extensions.name: Privileged Identity Management
extensions.detail: Just-in-time admin roles instead of standing privilege.
extensions.pricingNote: Needs Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance.

extensions.name: Entra ID Governance
extensions.detail: Lifecycle workflows, entitlement management, and access reviews.
extensions.pricingNote: A separate licence from P1 and P2.

compete.wins: The identity system you already have if the company lives in Microsoft 365.
compete.loses: A poor fit as the only identity layer for a large non-Microsoft SaaS estate.

name: Okta

source.title: Okta for Government High achieves FedRAMP High

description: Independent workforce identity with deep SaaS SSO and lifecycle automation.

extensions.name: Okta Workflows
extensions.detail: No-code joiner, mover, and leaver automation.

extensions.name: Adaptive MFA
extensions.detail: Step-up authentication based on device and risk signals.

extensions.name: Identity Threat Protection with Okta AI
extensions.detail: Continuous risk evaluation after sign-in, with session revocation when risk changes.

extensions.name: Identity Governance
extensions.detail: Access requests, certifications, and lifecycle automation; includes Workflows.

compete.wins: Deep SaaS single sign-on and lifecycle when identity is not only Microsoft.
compete.loses: A second identity bill on top of Entra, unless Entra cannot see the apps.

name: Ping Identity
description: Workforce and customer identity: SSO, MFA, and access policy, available as PingOne cloud or self-hosted software.

compete.wins: Handles hybrid and on-premises applications and complex federation that cloud-only tools struggle with.
compete.loses: More configuration than a simple SaaS SSO tool. Small teams with only SaaS apps will not use most of it.

name: CyberArk
description: Privileged access management: vaulting, rotation, and session control for admin and machine accounts. Part of Palo Alto Networks since 2026 and being brought into its Idira identity platform.

compete.wins: The established choice for controlling privileged accounts, with self-hosted and SaaS deployment.
compete.loses: Not a replacement for workforce SSO, and a full deployment is a long project. Watch how the move into Palo Alto changes licensing.

sources.title: Palo Alto Networks completes CyberArk acquisition (Techzine)
Palo Alto rebrands CyberArk with Idira (SDxCentral)

name: JumpCloud
description: Cloud directory with SSO, MFA, and device management for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

compete.wins: One tool for users and devices in a small company with no Active Directory.
compete.loses: Less depth than a dedicated identity platform for complex enterprise federation or governance.

name: Keycloak
description: Open-source identity and access management: SSO with OpenID Connect and SAML, user federation, and MFA.

compete.wins: No licence fee, and full control over where identity data lives.
compete.loses: You run it, patch it, and keep it highly available. It is not a managed workforce directory.

name: Defender for Office 365

source.title: Defender for Office 365 for US Government

description: Email and collaboration protection for phishing, malware, and safe links.

extensions.name: Attack simulation training
extensions.detail: Phishing simulations inside the Microsoft 365 tenant. Plan 2 only (E5 or add-on).

extensions.name: Safe Links
extensions.detail: Time-of-click URL detonation on mail and Teams links.

compete.wins: Phishing controls and attack simulation inside the Microsoft 365 tenant.
compete.loses: Does not replace a gateway if mail is not in Exchange Online.

name: Proofpoint Email Protection
description: Email security as a gateway, through an API on Microsoft 365, or both, with phishing, malware, and impersonation protection.

compete.wins: Deep threat intelligence and policy control for large or heavily targeted organisations.
compete.loses: Enterprise cost and administration. Smaller Microsoft 365 tenants may get enough from built-in protection.

name: Mimecast Email Security
description: Email security offered as a secure email gateway or as a cloud-integrated (API) service for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.

compete.wins: Gateway and API options from one vendor, with archiving and continuity available alongside.
compete.loses: The gateway model means changing mail routing. Compare against the API option and what the mail platform already includes.

name: Abnormal AI
description: API-based email security that models normal behaviour to catch phishing, business email compromise, and account takeover. Formerly Abnormal Security.

compete.wins: Adds to Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace through an API without changing mail routing.
compete.loses: A layer on top of the mail platform's own filtering, not a gateway replacement for on-premises mail.

name: Veeam
description: Backup and recovery for virtual, physical, and Microsoft 365 workloads.

extensions.name: Veeam ONE
extensions.detail: Monitoring and reporting on backup health and capacity.

extensions.name: Hardened repository
extensions.detail: Immutable backup target that resists ransomware deletion.

compete.wins: Restores virtual, physical, and Microsoft 365 data, with an immutable repository option.
compete.loses: Backup software is not a recovery plan. Untested restores do not count.

name: Rubrik
description: Backup and recovery for data centre, cloud, and SaaS data, with immutable backups and ransomware recovery tools.

compete.wins: Built around immutability and fast recovery, with threat detection on backup data.
compete.loses: Premium pricing. A small estate may not need its breadth.

name: Cohesity
description: Data protection for on-premises, cloud, and SaaS workloads, as software, appliances, or backup as a service. Merged with Veritas's data protection business in 2024.

compete.wins: Wide workload coverage and a choice of deployment models.
compete.loses: The Veritas merger means product lines are being combined. Confirm which product a quote covers.

name: Commvault

source.title: Commvault Cloud for Government FedRAMP High

description: Backup and disaster recovery across on-premises, cloud, databases, and SaaS, self-managed or as a service.

compete.wins: Very broad workload and storage support for complex estates.
compete.loses: Powerful but complex to design and run. Small teams may find it more than they need.

name: Druva
description: SaaS backup for Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, endpoints, and cloud workloads, with no backup infrastructure to run.

compete.wins: Nothing to deploy or patch, which suits small teams and SaaS-heavy companies.
compete.loses: Cloud-only. Large on-premises estates with tight recovery-time targets may prefer local copies.

name: Tenable

source.title: Tenable FedRAMP authorization for Tenable One

description: Vulnerability scanning and exposure management, from Nessus up to Tenable One.

extensions.name: Tenable OT Security
extensions.detail: Visibility for operational technology networks.

extensions.name: Tenable Cloud Security
extensions.detail: Cloud workload and entitlement exposure.

compete.wins: Broad vulnerability scanning from Nessus up to cloud and OT add-ons.
compete.loses: Skip it if Defender or Falcon already scans from the endpoint agent and you will not use the extra depth.

name: Qualys VMDR
description: Cloud vulnerability management with agent and network scanning, prioritisation, and optional patching.

compete.wins: A single cloud console for discovery, scanning, and patch tasks.
compete.loses: Licensed per asset and module, so costs grow with the estate and add-ons.

name: Rapid7 InsightVM
description: Vulnerability management with agent and network scanning, risk scoring, and remediation tracking.

compete.wins: Good remediation workflow and dashboards for teams that hand work to IT owners.
compete.loses: Overlaps with agent-based scanning if the EDR already reports vulnerabilities.

name: OpenVAS
description: Open-source network vulnerability scanner, with a free community edition and paid Greenbone products.

compete.wins: No licence fee for the community edition, and it can run fully offline.
compete.loses: The community feed and tooling need hands-on maintenance, and reporting is basic compared with commercial tools.

name: Defender for Cloud

source.title: Azure services in FedRAMP audit scope

description: Cloud security posture and workload protection, strongest inside Azure.

extensions.name: Defender CSPM
extensions.detail: Attack-path analysis and cloud security graph.

extensions.name: Workload plans
extensions.detail: Servers, containers, storage, and database protections.

compete.wins: The practical cloud posture tool when the estate is Azure.
compete.loses: Weaker across AWS and GCP than a cloud-only graph such as Wiz.

sources.title: Defender for Cloud multicloud support matrix

name: Wiz
description: Agentless cloud security graph for posture, identity, and toxic combinations. Owned by Google since 2026.

extensions.name: Wiz Code
extensions.detail: Shift-left scanning for repos and pipelines.

extensions.name: Wiz Defend
extensions.detail: Runtime detections on cloud workloads.

compete.wins: Agentless graph of identity, exposure, and toxic combinations across clouds.
compete.loses: High cost. Wrong buy for a single-cloud Azure estate that Defender for Cloud already sees.

sources.title: Google completes acquisition of Wiz (Cleary Gottlieb)

name: Cortex Cloud

source.title: Cortex Cloud FedRAMP High and Moderate

description: Cloud-native application protection platform: posture, workload, code-to-cloud, and runtime protection. Successor to Prisma Cloud.

compete.wins: Broad coverage from code to runtime for organisations already standardised on Palo Alto Networks.
compete.loses: Large and complex. Prisma Cloud customers face a migration to the new platform.

sources.title: Upgrade from Prisma Cloud to Cortex Cloud

name: Orca Security
description: Agentless cloud security platform covering posture, workload vulnerabilities, and data risk across AWS, Azure, and GCP.

compete.wins: Agentless setup gives full multi-cloud coverage quickly.
compete.loses: Agentless scanning is periodic. Add runtime protection if you need real-time workload detection.

name: Prowler
description: Open-source cloud security and compliance scanner for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, and more, with a paid hosted service.

compete.wins: Free, scriptable posture checks mapped to compliance frameworks.
compete.loses: Findings without a managed workflow. Someone has to schedule scans and drive fixes.

name: Zscaler
description: Zero trust exchange for web traffic and private application access.

extensions.name: Zscaler Private Access
extensions.detail: Broker user-to-app connections without network access.

extensions.name: ZDX
extensions.detail: Digital experience monitoring for SaaS and network paths.

compete.wins: Web and private-app access without a flat network.
compete.loses: A large project. Do not buy it to replace an endpoint agent.

name: Netskope One SSE
description: Security service edge: secure web gateway, CASB, zero trust private access, and data loss prevention in one cloud service.

compete.wins: Strong SaaS visibility and data protection alongside web and private-app access.
compete.loses: A large project, and the value depends on actually using the data protection features.

name: Prisma Access
description: Cloud-delivered SASE and SSE for web, SaaS, and private application access.

compete.wins: Fits well where Palo Alto firewalls and policy are already the standard.
compete.loses: Enterprise cost and complexity. Less attractive without the wider Palo Alto estate.

name: Cloudflare One
description: Zero trust access, secure web gateway, and CASB on Cloudflare's network. A free plan covers up to 50 users.

compete.wins: Free for small teams and simple to start, with pay-as-you-go pricing after that.
compete.loses: Advanced data protection and support need a contract plan. Check feature depth against enterprise needs.

sources.title: Cloudflare SASE and zero trust plans

name: Cisco Secure Access

source.title: Cisco Secure Access for Government FedRAMP High

description: Cisco's security service edge: secure web gateway, CASB, DNS security, and zero trust network access.

compete.wins: A natural step for organisations already using Cisco Umbrella, Duo, or Cisco networking.
compete.loses: Most compelling inside a Cisco estate. Compare packages carefully, because features vary by tier.

name: Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Private Access
description: Microsoft's security service edge: a secure web gateway (Internet Access) and zero trust access to private apps (Private Access), tied to Entra ID conditional access.

compete.wins: Uses the same Entra ID identities and conditional access policies, so it is a natural fit when identity is already Entra and it comes bundled in Entra Suite or Microsoft 365 E7.
compete.loses: Younger than the dedicated SSE vendors. Check data protection depth, branch connectivity, and non-Windows client support against Zscaler or Netskope before relying on it alone.

name: Burp Suite
description: Web security testing proxy used to inspect and attack application requests.

extensions.name: Burp Enterprise
extensions.detail: Scheduled scanning and CI integration for app teams.

extensions.name: Burp Collaborator
extensions.detail: Out-of-band interaction checks for blind vulnerabilities.

compete.wins: The standard proxy for testing a web app request by request.
compete.loses: A tester’s tool, not a scanner you can point at the company and walk away from.

name: ZAP
description: Open-source web application scanner and intercepting proxy, formerly OWASP ZAP. Its core team joined Checkmarx in 2024.

compete.wins: Free, automatable in CI, and good for baseline scans and manual testing.
compete.loses: Less polish and support than commercial scanners. Authenticated scans of complex apps take setup.

sources.title: ZAP has joined forces with Checkmarx

name: Invicti
description: Dynamic application and API security testing at scale, with proof-based confirmation of findings.

compete.wins: Scans many apps on a schedule and confirms many findings automatically, cutting false positives.
compete.loses: Enterprise cost. A team with a few apps may get further with Burp or ZAP.

name: StackHawk
description: Developer-focused dynamic testing for web apps and APIs, run in CI pipelines.

compete.wins: Fits engineering teams that want DAST results in the pull request.
compete.loses: Built for apps you develop and can run in a pipeline, not for scanning third-party sites.

name: Rapid7 InsightAppSec
description: Cloud dynamic application security testing for web apps and APIs, with an optional managed service.

compete.wins: Pairs with InsightVM for teams already on Rapid7.
compete.loses: Most useful inside the Rapid7 platform. Compare scan depth against specialist DAST vendors.

name: Snyk
description: Developer security for open-source dependencies, code, containers, and IaC.

extensions.name: Snyk Code
extensions.detail: SAST in the IDE and pull request.

extensions.name: Snyk Container
extensions.detail: Image and base-image vulnerability scanning.

extensions.name: Snyk IaC
extensions.detail: Misconfiguration checks for Terraform and Kubernetes.

compete.wins: Finds vulnerable dependencies, code, containers, and IaC in the developer workflow.
compete.loses: Does not test a running web app the way Burp does. They are not substitutes.

name: Checkmarx

source.title: Checkmarx One for Government FedRAMP Moderate

description: Enterprise application security platform covering static analysis, open-source dependency analysis, and API and IaC scanning.

compete.wins: Deep static analysis across many languages, aimed at large engineering organizations with a dedicated application security team.
compete.loses: Enterprise cost and real tuning effort. Too heavy for a small team that only needs dependency and basic code scanning.

name: Veracode
description: Cloud-delivered application security testing: static analysis, open-source dependency analysis, and dynamic scanning, with policy reporting.

compete.wins: Policy and compliance reporting built for audits and customer reviews. Can scan compiled binaries when source code is not available.
compete.loses: Enterprise cost, and code or binaries are uploaded to the vendor's cloud for scanning, which some teams cannot allow.

name: SonarQube
description: Code quality and static security analysis, with a free self-hosted community edition and paid tiers.

compete.wins: Free to start and already familiar to many developers. Quality gates run in the build pipeline.
compete.loses: The free edition's security analysis is limited. Deeper security rules and some languages need a paid edition.

name: Semgrep
description: Pattern-based static analysis. The Community Edition engine is open source (LGPL 2.1); the cross-file Pro engine, managed rules, secrets, and supply-chain scanning are paid.

compete.wins: Fast scans and rules a developer can read and write. The engine is free.
compete.loses: Cross-file analysis, managed rules, and secrets scanning are in the paid platform. The community rules carry a licence limited to internal business use, and someone has to own the rules.

name: GitHub Secret Protection & Code Security
description: Secret scanning (Secret Protection) and CodeQL code scanning with dependency review (Code Security), built into GitHub. Core features are free on public repositories.

compete.wins: No separate tool if the code already lives in GitHub. Findings appear in the pull request.
compete.loses: Only helps repositories hosted on GitHub. On private repositories each product is billed per active committer per month.

name: Black Duck
description: Open-source component and license analysis, with Coverity static analysis and other testing in the same portfolio (formerly Synopsys Software Integrity).

compete.wins: Strong open-source license and component analysis, often used for software bills of materials and due diligence.
compete.loses: Enterprise cost, and the portfolio is several products rather than one developer workflow.

name: OpenText Fortify
description: Static and dynamic application security testing, available on-premises or as a hosted service.

compete.wins: Long-established static analyzer with broad language coverage, and it can run fully on-premises.
compete.loses: Needs dedicated staff to deploy and tune. A large commitment for a team without an application security function.

name: Atomic Red Team
description: Open library of small tests mapped to adversary techniques.

extensions.name: Invoke-AtomicRedTeam
extensions.detail: PowerShell runner that executes the test library locally.

compete.wins: Free, repeatable tests that show whether a detection fires.
compete.loses: Someone has to run it and read the result. It is not a managed red team.

name: Caldera
description: Open-source automated adversary emulation platform from MITRE, now hosted under the Apache organisation, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.

compete.wins: Free, with automated multi-step operations and plugins.
compete.loses: Needs someone who can build and read operations. It is a framework, not a service.

name: Stratus Red Team
description: Open-source tool that runs cloud attack techniques in AWS, Azure, GCP, and Kubernetes to test detections.

compete.wins: Free, focused tests for cloud detections, each with setup and cleanup.
compete.loses: Cloud-only, and someone has to check whether alerts fired.

name: SCYTHE
description: Commercial adversary emulation platform for building and running realistic attack campaigns.

compete.wins: Lets red and purple teams build custom campaigns without writing their own tools.
compete.loses: Needs an operator. Small teams may get the same answer from free frameworks.

name: Pentera
description: Automated security validation that executes real attack techniques inside the network.

extensions.name: Credential exposure
extensions.detail: Validates leaked or cracked credentials against live systems.

extensions.name: RansomwareReady
extensions.detail: Tests paths an encryption attack would actually take.

compete.wins: Runs real attack paths inside the network and shows which controls failed.
compete.loses: High cost. Atomic Red Team answers the same question if a person will run the tests.

name: AttackIQ
description: Breach and attack simulation that runs attack scenarios against production controls, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.

compete.wins: Continuous, repeatable tests of whether controls detect and block.
compete.loses: Needs ongoing ownership to act on results. An unread dashboard does not raise maturity.

name: SafeBreach
description: Breach and attack simulation with a large library of attack scenarios.

compete.wins: Broad scenario coverage for testing many controls on a schedule.
compete.loses: Enterprise cost, and value depends on a team fixing what it finds.

name: Cymulate
description: Exposure validation platform combining breach and attack simulation with attack-surface and control testing.

compete.wins: Modular, so a team can start with the tests it needs most.
compete.loses: The module menu makes quotes hard to compare. Check exactly what is included.

name: Picus
description: Security control validation with attack simulation and vendor-specific mitigation guidance.

compete.wins: Gives fixes written for the specific security products in place.
compete.loses: Most useful when someone will apply the mitigations it suggests.

name: NodeZero
description: Autonomous penetration testing that chains real attack paths across internal, external, and cloud networks.

compete.wins: Can be run as often as needed without booking a pentest firm.
compete.loses: Not a substitute for a human tester's judgement on business logic and scope.

name: KnowBe4
description: Security awareness training and simulated phishing for the whole company.

extensions.name: PhishER
extensions.detail: Shared inbox triage for user-reported phishing.

extensions.name: Compliance Plus
extensions.detail: Extra modules for regulated training content.

compete.wins: Phishing simulation and training for the whole company.
compete.loses: Overlaps with Microsoft attack simulation training if Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 is already licensed and used.

name: Proofpoint ZenGuide
description: Risk-based security awareness training and phishing simulation, linked to Proofpoint email threat data.

compete.wins: Targets training at the people email data shows are attacked most.
compete.loses: Strongest alongside Proofpoint email security. Less of an edge on its own.

name: Hoxhunt
description: Adaptive phishing training that adjusts difficulty to each person and rewards reporting.

compete.wins: Focuses on building the habit of reporting, not just completion rates.
compete.loses: Narrower content library than the largest training vendors.

name: Mimecast Engage
description: Security awareness training and human risk scoring from Mimecast.

compete.wins: Combines training with risk scores from Mimecast email data.
compete.loses: Most value alongside Mimecast email security.

name: Gophish
description: Open-source phishing simulation framework you host yourself.

compete.wins: Free, and full control over simulation content and data.
compete.loses: Phishing simulation only, with no training content. You host it and manage sending reputation.

name: Vanta
description: Automated evidence collection for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and similar audits.

extensions.name: Trust Center
extensions.detail: Customer-facing security page fed by live controls.

extensions.name: Vendor Risk Management
extensions.detail: Questionnaires and reviews for third parties.

compete.wins: Collects evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and similar reviews without a spreadsheet.
compete.loses: Not an enterprise risk register. Once risk, audit, and policy work span many business units, a GRC platform does that job.

name: Drata
description: Compliance automation with continuous control monitoring across SOC 2, ISO 27001, and many other frameworks.

compete.wins: Broad framework coverage and integrations for continuous evidence.
compete.loses: Like its peers, it collects evidence. It does not make the controls work.

name: Secureframe
description: Compliance automation for SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, CMMC, and others, with policy templates and evidence collection.

compete.wins: Covers several regulated frameworks beyond SOC 2, including CMMC and PCI DSS.
compete.loses: Overlaps heavily with Vanta and Drata. Compare integrations and auditor fit, not marketing.

name: Sprinto
description: Compliance automation aimed at startups and growing companies, with continuous monitoring for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and more.

compete.wins: Often priced for smaller companies getting a first certification.
compete.loses: Less suited to complex, multi-entity enterprise programs.

name: Thoropass
description: Compliance automation bundled with audit services, so readiness and the audit are bought together.

compete.wins: One contract for the platform and the audit, which can simplify a first SOC 2.
compete.loses: Bundling ties you to its audit partners. Teams that want to choose their own auditor lose that freedom.

name: ServiceNow IRM
description: Integrated risk management for policies, risks, issues, and audit work.

extensions.name: Policy and Compliance
extensions.detail: Control testing and citation mapping inside the IRM suite.

extensions.name: Risk Management
extensions.detail: Enterprise risk register with scoring and workflows.

compete.wins: Policies, risks, and audit findings in one system of record.
compete.loses: Enterprise cost and an implementation. A mid-market SOC 2 program does not need it.

name: Archer
description: Integrated risk management for enterprise, operational, IT, and third-party risk, audit, and compliance.

compete.wins: Long-established and highly configurable for large, regulated programs.
compete.loses: Heavy implementation and administration. Usually needs dedicated staff or partners.

name: Optro
description: Connected audit, risk, infosec compliance, and IT risk platform. Formerly AuditBoard, renamed in March 2026.

compete.wins: Strong with internal audit and SOX teams, and quicker to adopt than heavier GRC suites.
compete.loses: Its roots are in audit. Check depth for security operations and third-party risk needs.

name: OneTrust Tech Risk & Compliance
description: IT risk and compliance management, part of a wider platform that also covers privacy and third-party risk.

compete.wins: Useful where privacy, third-party risk, and security compliance should share one platform.
compete.loses: Modules are sold separately. The full value depends on buying several of them.

name: LogicGate Risk Cloud
description: No-code GRC platform for building risk, compliance, and third-party risk workflows.

compete.wins: Workflows can be configured without developers.
compete.loses: Flexibility means design work. Plan time to model the program before go-live.
